title: DFS in Porto: Find the route like a maze pro
description: Watch Depth-First Search (DFS) explore Porto’s street network by diving deep along paths before backtracking. This visualization shows how DFS traverses a graph and what that means for reaching a target efficiently.
ig_caption:
🗺️🌊 Porto (Matosinhos) street map + DFS = deep, twisty exploration!

In this visualization, **DFS (Depth-First Search)** starts from the origin node and **keeps going forward** along adjacent streets (neighbors) as far as possible, only **backtracking** when it hits a dead end. In graph-theory terms, the road network is modeled as a graph **G(V, E)** where intersections are vertices **V** and street segments are edges **E**—DFS performs a traversal using a **stack (explicit or implicit via recursion)**.

⚙️ Key intuition: DFS doesn’t guarantee the shortest path—its behavior depends on **neighbor ordering** and the structure of the map. That’s why you’ll see it “go deep” first, then retrace steps when needed.

✅ Want to see DFS vs BFS on the same map? Comment **“BFS”** and hit follow for more real-world algorithm visuals!

fb_caption:
🚦 How does a computer “think” about roads? Using **DFS (Depth-First Search)**, we treat the streets of Porto (Matosinhos) like a **graph**: intersections are nodes and roads are edges. DFS explores by going deep along one route, then **backtracking**—a classic graph search strategy used to traverse and analyze network structure.
